title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on How to Handle Divorce Procedures for Chinese Students Abroad Where Both Spouses Request Divorce

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Court
Notice on How to Handle Divorce Procedures for Chinese Overseas Students Who Both Request Divorce
(85) Min Ta Zi No. 38
×××, ×××:
We have received your letter regarding the request for dissolution of the marital relationship. According to the relevant provisions of Chinese law, if both parties have no dispute over divorce, property division, child support, or other issues, you may return to China and apply for divorce procedures with the original marriage registration authority; if there is any dispute over the above issues, you must return to China and file a divorce lawsuit with the People's Court at the place of original marriage registration. If both parties are unable to return to China due to special circumstances, you may execute a power of attorney, entrusting a domestic relative, friend, or lawyer as an agent to handle the matter on your behalf, and submit written opinions to the original domestic marriage registration authority or the People's Court at the place of original marriage registration, where the registration authority shall handle the matter or the People's Court shall conduct the trial. The power of attorney and written opinions shall be notarized by a local notary authority and certified by the Chinese embassy or consulate in the United States, or may be directly notarized by the Chinese embassy or consulate in the United States.
December 31, 1985
